prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the open outdoor baseball field as a smooth vertical brightness gradient along the ground plane from very bright near the camera wearer (1–2 m below the viewpoint) to dark grey at the distant tree line (>30 m ahead) and black in the sky above. In frames 1 to 4, as the camera wearer walks forward and reduces the distance to two people standing near the center of the dirt infield from roughly 12 m to 6 m, the pair appears as mid-grey silhouettes standing within 1 m (arm's reach) of each other while nothing is within arm's reach of the camera wearer. In frames 1 to 3, the grey-shirted person on the right faces away and stands slightly in front of the dark-shirted person on the left, partially occluding them, before both separate in frame 4 as the left person faces toward the camera wearer and the right person turns left. In frame 5, the camera wearer turns sharply left and tilts down toward the ground, shifting the two people completely out of view to the right while revealing a dimly visible vertical light pole and bleachers on the left. Compared to the uniform tan dirt in the RGB image, the depth map makes the continuous ground-plane recession and the foreground separation of the pair against the dark trees much clearer, though it is unreliable at separating the two overlapping bodies in frames 1 to 3, blends their lower legs and feet into the ground depth, and introduces white masking artifacts in the upper corners.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the two people standing near the center of the infield in frames 1 to 4 as distinct pink and brown masks labeled 'person' on a black background, growing in size as the camera wearer approaches them from about 12 m down to 6 m. Across frames 1 to 3, the masks show the person on the right standing slightly in front of and partially occluding the person on the left while both face away from the camera wearer and remain within arm's reach (<1 m) of each other, before they stand side-by-side unoccluded in frame 4 with the left person facing the camera wearer and the right person facing left. Nothing is within arm's reach of the camera wearer in any frame, and in frame 5 the map is completely empty because the camera turns left and leaves both people out of view beyond the right edge. Unlike the RGB image and depth map where the overlapping figures and dark clothing blend against the dark background trees in frames 1 to 3, the segmentation map cleanly separates the two individuals into distinct instances and also flags a tiny distant object ('c...') partially clipped at the far right edge of frame 1. However, the map is unreliable in omitting all ground, fence, bleacher, and tree layout context, swapping the pink and brown instance IDs between the two people in frame 4, and failing to re-detect the far-right edge object after frame 1.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely black across all five frames, failing to detect any yellow body keypoints or magenta hand keypoints in the scene. In the RGB context, two people stand on the open infield roughly 12 m ahead of the camera wearer in frame 1 and approach to about 6 m by frame 4 while staying within arm's reach (<1 m) of each other, before disappearing out of view to the right when the camera turns left in frame 5. Although RGB shows the nearer person on the right facing away and partially occluding the second person in frames 1 to 3, and then shows the left person facing toward the camera wearer with hands on hips beside the left-facing right person in frame 4, none of these postures or orientations are captured in the pose map. The empty map indirectly confirms that no person or extended hand is within arm's reach or close foreground range of the camera wearer, whose own body remains below and behind the camera's field of view. Consequently, the pose map adds nothing that is hard to see in the RGB strip and is completely unreliable at distances of 6 to 12 m where the subjects occupy too few pixels for skeleton extraction.
